doc.title: Håkan Rydin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016

title: Swedish baritone saxophonist Lars Gullin
summary: Rydin praises Gullin as a composer who blended Nordic classical influence into jazz, with a tragic life.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Any Swedish musicians that you particularly took note of?

Yes. I will mention one specifically. Of course there are many. There’s Lars Gullin. And he was a little bit famous even in the States. He was on the Down Beat list. And what he did, in the 50s and 60s, he was influenced by the Nordic classical music. And maybe

that’s not so very unique, especially later. But what he wrote songs inspired by that music but he made it into genuine jazz. Songs that were nice to play on, nice to improvise on. He really was a great composer. Fantastic musician, with a tragic life I’m sorry to say, but some great songs he wrote. At least in his early days he was a very melodic saxophone player like Stan Getz — not really — but very melodic and very beautiful.
